## Covered in this lecture

# Simple Linear Regression

## Setup

::: {.incremental}

- Predict $Y$ on a single predictor variable $X$
$$
Y \approx \beta_0 + \beta_1 X
$$
- "$\approx$" .... "is approximately modeled as"

:::

## Example

:::::: {.columns}

::::: {.column width="30%"}

![screenshot of the advertising data set](../../Figures/AdvertisingDataSet-Screenshot.png){fig-alt="screenshot of the advertising data set" width="70%"}

:::::

::::: {.column width="40%"}

$$
sales \approx \beta_0 + \beta_1 TV
$$

- $\beta_0$ intercept; $\beta_1$ slope
- Coefficients or parameters: $\{\beta_0, \beta_1\}$
- Once we have good guesses for $\hat \beta_i$, model is
$$
\hat y = \hat \beta_0 + \hat \beta_1 x
$$

:::::

::::::

## Least squares criterion: Setup

### How do we estimate the coefficients?

:::::: {.columns}

::::: {.column width="40%"}

- Given $(x_1,y_1),\cdots,(x_n,y_n)$
- Let $\hat y_i = \hat \beta_0 + \hat \beta_1 x_i$ be the prediction for $Y$ at the $i$th value of $X$.
- $e_i = y_i - \hat y_i$ is the $i$th residual

:::::

::::: {.column width="40%"}

![scatter plot with linear fit and residuals](../../Figures/Fig3-1.png){fig-alt="scatter plot with linear fit and residuals" width="70%"}

:::::

::::::

## Least squares criterion: RSS

:::::: {.columns}

::::: {.column width="60%"}

![scatter plot of sales versus TV advertising with least-squares fit and residual line segments](../../Figures/Fig3-2.png){fig-alt="Scatter plot of sales versus TV advertising spending with a least-squares regression line through the data; a vertical gray line segment connects each data point to the fitted line, representing that point's residual" width="70%"}
$$
sales \approx \beta_0 + \beta_1 TV
$$

:::::

::::: {.column width="34%"}

Residual sum of squares RSS is
$$
\begin{aligned}
RSS &= e_1^2 + \cdots + e_n^2\\
    &= \sum_i (y_i - \hat \beta_0 - \hat \beta_1 x_i)^2
\end{aligned}
$$

:::::

::::::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Least squares criterion"}

Find $\beta_0$ and $\beta_1$ that minimize the RSS.

:::

## Least squares coefficient estimates

:::::: {.columns}

::::: {.column width="40%"}

Minimizing RSS:

$$
\min_{\beta_0,\beta_1} \sum_i (y_i - \hat \beta_0 - \hat \beta_1 x_i)^2
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial RSS}{\partial \hat \beta_0} & = -2 \sum_i (y_i - \hat{\beta}_0 - \hat{\beta}_1x_i) = 0 \\
\frac{\partial RSS}{\partial \hat \beta_1} & = -2 \sum_i x_i(y_i - \hat \beta_0 - \hat \beta_1x_i) = 0
\end{aligned}
$$

:::::

::::: {.column width="40%"}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\hat \beta_1 &= \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i-\overline x) (y_i - \overline y)}
                     {\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline x)^2}\\
\hat \beta_0 &= \overline y - \hat \beta_1 \overline x
\end{aligned}
$$

- Closed form!
- Though iterative methods (e.g. gradient descent) are often used for larger problems

:::::
